correctness.rationale: The connected path plus a positive total sink makes M positive definite even when background loss is zero. The end-to-end cofactor is the invariant k², so concentration minimization is determinant maximization. Strict fixed-middle endpoint balancing reduces to u, strict log-det concavity proves global uniqueness, and exact endpoint derivative signs give F_c=sqrt(v²+4kv)-v with equality correctly at a unique boundary optimum. The quadratic stationarity root and two-room comparison are explicit. The standalone program passed 54,269 supplementary checks; sampling is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Three rooms is the smallest communicating path with an intermediate room. The model answers a natural policy question—when can any fixed total removal budget profitably be allocated to that transit room rather than split between pollutant source and exposure receptor? It exhibits a sharp baseline-loss-dependent support change absent from the two-room counterpart, a closed-form optimum at every budget and a nontrivial endpoint dominance law. These predictions give an exact low-dimensional benchmark against which numerical multi-zone design tools can be checked; they are not field-calibrated prescriptions.
